questions.q: What does the psalmist say about the temple of Yahweh?
questions.a: He says the temple of Yahweh is a wonderful place.

questions.q: For what does the psalmist long?
questions.a: He longs to be in the courtyards of Yahweh’s temple.

questions.q: To whom does the psalmist’s whole being cry out?
questions.a: His whole being cries out to the only true God.

questions.q: Where has the sparrow built her house and the swallow a nest where she may lay her young?
questions.a: They have built their house and nest near the temple of Yahweh, commander of heavenly armies.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about those who live by Yahweh’s temple?
questions.a: They will live a good life and worship Yahweh in his temple continually.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about the man whose strength is in Yahweh?
questions.a: The people whom Yahweh has made strong enough to travel to the temple will have a good life.

questions.q: What do those who pass through the Valley of Baca do to it?
questions.a: They dig wells for water, and God sends the early rain to fill those wells with life-giving water.

questions.q: What happens to those who arrive at the temple of God?
questions.a: They become stronger as they go.

questions.q: Who does the psalmist want to hear his prayer?
questions.a: He wants Yahweh, God of Armies, to hear his prayer.

questions.q: Who does the psalmist want to listen to what he is saying?
questions.a: He wants the God whom Jacob’s descendants worship to listen to what he is saying and do what he is asking.

questions.q: How does the psalmist ask God to treat the anointed king?
questions.a: He asks God to treat favorably the king he has appointed to protect his people.

questions.q: A day in Yahweh’s courts is better than what?
questions.a: A day in Yahweh’s temple courts is better than a thousand spent anywhere else.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say he would rather do than dwell in the tents of wickedness?
questions.a: He would rather stand at the entrance to the courtyard of God’s temple than stay in any of the comfortable homes where wicked people live.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do for his people?
questions.a: Yahweh makes them prosper, protects them, is kind to them, honors them, and gives them every good thing that they need.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about the man who trusts in Yahweh of Armies?
questions.a: The man who trusts in Yahweh of Armies is happy.

commentary.text: The psalmist expresses his affection to the ordinances of God.
His desire towards the God of the ordinances.

Verses 1–7 The ordinances of God are the believer's solace in this evil world; in them he enjoys the presence of the living God: this causes him to regret his absence from them. They are to his soul as the nest to the bird. Yet they are only an earnest of the happiness of heaven; but how can men desire to enter that holy habitation, who complain of Divine ordinances as wearisome? Those are truly happy, who go forth, and go on in the exercise of religion, in the strength of the grace of Jesus Christ, from whom all our sufficiency is. The pilgrims to the heavenly city may have to pass through many a valley of weeping, and many a thirsty desert; but wells of salvation shall be opened for them, and consolations sent for their support. Those that press forward in their Christian course, shall find God add grace to their graces. And those who grow in grace, shall be perfect in glory.

In all our addresses to God, we must desire that he would look on Christ, his Anointed One, and accept us for his sake: we must look to Him with faith, and then God will with favour look upon the face of the Anointed: we, without him, dare not show our faces. The psalmist pleads love to God's ordinances. Let us account one day in God's courts better than a thousand spent elsewhere; and deem the meanest place in his service preferable to the highest earthly preferment. We are here in darkness, but if God be our God, he will be to us a Sun, to enlighten and enliven us, to guide and direct us. We are here in danger, but he will be to us a Shield, to secure us from the fiery darts that fly thick about us. Through he has not promised to give riches and dignities, he has promised to give grace and glory to all that seek them in his appointed way. And what is grace, but heaven begun below, in the knowledge, love, and service of God? What is glory, but the completion of this happiness, in being made like to him, and in fully enjoying him for ever? Let it be our care to walk uprightly, and then let us trust God to give us every thing that is good for us. If we cannot go to the house of the Lord, we may go by faith to the Lord of the house; in him we shall be happy, and may be easy. That man is really happy, whatever his outward circumstances may be, who trusts in the Lord of hosts, the God of Jacob.
